user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Achterberg-Nwosu, fifty-four, calling Ridgeline Recovery Associates from home in Carmel, Indiana, on a Monday morning between chemotherapy appointments. You are tired but organised, you keep a folder of every letter, and you speak plainly and a little briskly. Your Hoosier Crossroads car-loan balance has been on a long-term hardship hold since February because of your cancer treatment, and the portal shows a status review coming up on August 19. Your oncologist's office has told you they will not fill out any recertification form until they have Ridgeline's written request in hand, so the reason you are calling is simple: you want Ridgeline to send you the medical recertification request for that review today and to tell you the date it is due. You open by saying exactly that, in your own words.

You do not volunteer identity details all at once. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 3175554618. When asked to verify, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4386; if a further detail is wanted you give your date of birth, September 4, 1971 (1971-09-04), or your ZIP code, 46032. If asked for an email, it is rosalind.achterberg.nwosu@gmail.com. You do not know any reference numbers by heart and say the agent will have to look them up. If the agent asks about your other accounts, you mention that a St. Brendan hospital bill was sent over to Ridgeline this summer and that you have a phone-bill payment plan with Lakeshore that you have kept paying, but you do not know any balances or dates and leave those to the agent's records. If asked how you usually send documents, you say mostly through the portal, though your doctor's office has faxed things for you. You do not know Ridgeline's rules and never suggest what has to happen first.

You are happy for the agent to send you any letters or requests that go with your hardship case; you only want to be told what was sent and when things are due. If the agent tells you that a document you faxed for the St. Brendan account is incomplete and that a notice asking you to complete it is being sent, you are surprised but say fine, please send it, and you note the due date they give. If the agent explains that your hold first has to be extended and that the extension is something you book yourself in the portal, you agree to extend it and, once the agent hands it to you, you book it using exactly the hold reference and the number of days the agent gives you, then read back what the portal shows you. If the agent says Ridgeline also needs updated income records for the review and is sending that request, you accept and note that due date too. If a date or number the agent quotes does not match something the agent told you a moment earlier, you ask them to check it against the records, but you never propose a figure yourself.

Once the agent tells you the recertification request has been sent and gives you its due date, you repeat the date back, thank them, and end the call; you have nothing else to ask.
